# Notebook 00 -- Ingest the LSTM benchmark projections

**What this notebook does (H5 / Objective 5).** Ingests CAMELS-IND-Proj
(Singh et al. 2026, Zenodo 21775597, CC BY 4.0) -- 13 CMIP6 GCMs x 4 SSPs
daily LSTM streamflow 2015--2100 for 472 Peninsular-India catchments (hydroDL
package; historical per-GCM streamflow included) -- as the **Track B
benchmark object only** (AGENTS.md, two-track design fixed 18 Nov 2026):

* Track B is the *audited object of H5* -- never substrate, never input to
  our models, and **LSTM series are never treated as observed truth**;
* their forcings inherit the Mishra et al. (2020) South-Asia bias correction
  (documented in their data description) -- one more reason they can never
  be our substrate (our Track A correction is catchment-tuned, seasonal,
  out-of-sample-ranked).

Steps:

1. **Integrity + unpacking**: verify the downloaded zip's exact byte size and
   CRC (`unzip -t`), then unzip once into `D:/Datasets/CAMELS_IND_Proj/extract/`.
2. **Structure discovery** (no hardcoded layout): walk the extracted tree,
   write `data_processed/bench/zip_inventory.csv` (relative path, size, depth,
   guessed role), and **verify the "239 confidence-flagged catchments" claim**
   from the project brief against what is actually inside (the data-description
   PDF's file-structure diagram is an embedded image -- not text-extractable --
   so the claim is checked here, in the data, not in prose).
3. **Extraction**: for every Tier 1/2 catchment in the HYD roster x every
   GCM x every SSP, pull the daily LSTM streamflow 2015--2100, convert
   **cumecs -> mm/day** with the CAMELS-IND catchment area (the same
   `area_km2` used by GR4J/GR6J), and cache one rds per catchment under
   `data_processed/bench/q_lstm/<id>.rds`. Unit conversion and any skipped
   catchment are logged with reason codes -- no silent drops.
4. **Provenance stamp**: every cached series carries `source =
   "CAMELS-IND-Proj LSTM (Track B benchmark)"`, the zenodo DOI, the GCM/SSP
   key, and the unit-conversion constants -- the H5 evaluator (BENCH_10)
   consumes these caches only.

```{r log-file}
bench_output_dir <- file.path(hyd_project_root, "data_processed", "bench")
dir.create(bench_output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
bench_log_file <- file.path(bench_output_dir, "bench_00_log.txt")
bench_log <- function(msg) {
   line <- paste0(format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), " | ", msg)
   cat(line, "\n"); cat(line, "\n", file = bench_log_file, append = TRUE)
}
```

## 1. Configuration

```{r config}
bench_zip_fp   <- "D:/Datasets/CAMELS_IND_Proj/CAMELS-IND-Proj_data.zip"
bench_extract  <- "D:/Datasets/CAMELS_IND_Proj/extract"
bench_expected_bytes <- 11293105215L   # Zenodo record 21775597 file size
bench_test_mode <- FALSE               # TRUE: 3 catchments x 2 GCMs x 1 SSP
```

## 2. Zip integrity + one-time unpack

```{r unzip, eval=TRUE}
stopifnot(file.exists(bench_zip_fp))
zip_size <- as.double(file.size(bench_zip_fp))
bench_log(paste0("zip size on disk: ", zip_size, " bytes (expected ",
                 bench_expected_bytes, ")"))
# Multi-connection downloaders (aria2c) write sparse segments ahead of the
# completed bytes, so an almost-full file size proves nothing. Two guards:
#   (a) no aria2 control file may remain (it exists while downloading),
#   (b) the archive must pass a real integrity test before unpacking.
aria2_ctrl <- paste0(bench_zip_fp, ".aria2")
if (file.exists(aria2_ctrl)) stop(paste0(
   "download still in progress: aria2 control file present (", aria2_ctrl,
   "). Wait for aria2c to exit cleanly."))
if (zip_size < bench_expected_bytes) stop(paste0(
   "zip incomplete: ", zip_size, " < ", bench_expected_bytes,
   " bytes -- resume the download before running BENCH_00"))
bench_log("running zip integrity test (unzip -t) ...")
test_out <- system2("unzip", c("-t", shQuote(bench_zip_fp)),
                    stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE)
test_status <- attr(test_out, "status")
if (!is.null(test_status) && test_status != 0) stop(paste0(
   "zip integrity test FAILED (unzip -t exit ", test_status, "): ",
   paste(utils::tail(test_out, 3), collapse = " | ")))
bench_log("zip integrity test passed")

if (!dir.exists(bench_extract)) {
   utils::unzip(bench_zip_fp, exdir = bench_extract, overwrite = FALSE)
   bench_log("unzip complete")
} else {
   bench_log("extract dir already present -- skipping unzip")
}
```

## 3. Structure discovery + the "239 confidence flags" claim check

```{r discovery, eval=TRUE}
all_files <- list.files(bench_extract, recursive = TRUE, include.dirs = FALSE)
inv <- data.table::data.table(
   rel_path = all_files,
   size_bytes = vapply(file.path(bench_extract, all_files), file.size,
                       numeric(1)),
   depth = vapply(strsplit(all_files, "/"), length, integer(1)),
   ext = tools::file_ext(all_files))
inv[, top_dir := vapply(strsplit(rel_path, "/"), `[`, character(1), 1)]
inv[, n_path_tokens := vapply(strsplit(rel_path, "/"), length, integer(1))]
data.table::fwrite(inv, file.path(bench_output_dir, "zip_inventory.csv"))

cat("extracted files:", nrow(inv), "\n")
cat("top-level entries:\n"); print(sort(unique(inv$top_dir)))
cat("extensions:\n");        print(table(inv$ext, useNA = "ifany"))

# claim check: the project brief says "239 confidence-flagged catchments".
# Look for any confidence/flag/nan-related filename or column evidence.
conf_hits <- inv[grepl("confid|flag|nan|mask|qual", rel_path,
                       ignore.case = TRUE), rel_path]
if (length(conf_hits)) {
   cat("confidence/flag-like files found:\n"); print(conf_hits)
   bench_log(paste0("claim check: confidence-like files present: ",
                    paste(conf_hits, collapse = "; ")))
} else {
   cat("NO confidence/flag-like file found in the zip -- the '239",
       "confidence-flagged catchments' brief claim must be re-scored\n")
   bench_log("claim check: NO confidence-like file found (brief claim unsupported by filenames; check column headers of the streamflow CSVs before final verdict)")
}

# GCM x SSP discovery from the path tokens (adapt to whatever tokens exist)
path_tokens <- table(unlist(strsplit(inv$rel_path, "/")))
cat("most frequent path tokens:\n")
print(utils::head(sort(path_tokens, decreasing = TRUE), 40))
```

## 4. Extract per-catchment LSTM series (cumecs -> mm/day)

```{r extract, eval=TRUE}
# roster: HYD Tier 1/2 catchments with the area attribute used everywhere
inputs_sum <- data.table::fread(file.path(hyd_output_dir,
                                          "hyd_inputs_summary.csv"),
                                colClasses = list(character = "id"))
roster <- inputs_sum[, .(id, area_km2)]
if (bench_test_mode) roster <- roster[1:3]

q_dir <- file.path(bench_output_dir, "q_lstm")
dir.create(q_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

excl <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(roster))) {
   id <- roster$id[i]; area <- roster$area_km2[i]
   res <- tryCatch({
      # locate this catchment's streamflow files in the discovered tree:
      # match on the gauge id token, then keep streamflow-like paths
      hits <- inv[grepl(id, rel_path, fixed = TRUE) &
                     grepl("streamflow|flow|Q", rel_path, ignore.case = TRUE),
                  rel_path]
      if (!length(hits)) {
         excl[[length(excl) + 1L]] <- data.table::data.table(
            module = "BENCH_00", catchment = id, reason_code = "not_found_in_zip",
            detail = NA_character_)
         "missing"
      } else {
         # read + convert + cache (per GCM x SSP, layout discovered above)
         store <- list()
         for (h in hits) {
            fp <- file.path(bench_extract, h)
            dt <- data.table::fread(fp, colClasses = list(character = 1))
            setnames(dt, 1, "date")
            val_cols <- setdiff(names(dt), "date")
            # cumecs -> mm/day: Q[mm/d] = Q[m3/s] * 86400 / (area_km2 * 1e6) * 1000
            for (vc in val_cols)
               dt[, (vc) := get(vc) * 86.4 / area]
            store[[h]] <- dt
         }
         saveRDS(list(id = id, area_km2 = area,
                      source = "CAMELS-IND-Proj LSTM (Track B benchmark)",
                      doi = "10.5281/zenodo.21775597",
                      unit = "mm/day (converted from cumecs, factor 86.4/area_km2)",
                      series = store),
                 file.path(q_dir, paste0(id, ".rds")))
         "ok"
      }
   }, error = function(e) {
      excl[[length(excl) + 1L]] <- data.table::data.table(
         module = "BENCH_00", catchment = id, reason_code = "read_error",
         detail = conditionMessage(e))
      "error"
   })
   if (i %% 25 == 0) cat("  ...", i, "of", nrow(roster), "\n")
}

excl_dt <- data.table::rbindlist(excl, use.names = TRUE, fill = TRUE)
if (nrow(excl_dt)) {
   data.table::fwrite(excl_dt, file.path(hyd_project_root, "data_processed",
                                         "logs", "BENCH_00_exclusions.csv"))
}
n_cached <- length(list.files(q_dir, pattern = "\\.rds$"))
bench_log(paste0("BENCH_00 done: cached ", n_cached, " catchments | excluded ",
                 nrow(excl_dt)))
cat("cached:", n_cached, "| excluded:", nrow(excl_dt), "\n")
```

## Take-away

- `data_processed/bench/q_lstm/<id>.rds` -- per-catchment LSTM series cache
  (all GCMs x SSPs, mm/day, provenance-stamped, Track B benchmark only).
- `zip_inventory.csv` -- the discovered structure (auditable; no hardcoded
  layout assumptions survived into the extraction code).
- The "239 confidence-flagged catchments" brief claim is scored here, in
  data, and recorded in `bench_00_log.txt` -- `BENCH_10_lowflow_eval.Rmd`
  computes the low-flow metric suite on these series (same `metric_version
  v1` definitions) and writes `h5_verdict.md` against the pre-registered H5
  rule (LSTM does NOT uniformly beat GR4J/GR6J at low flows).
